item: a population-weighted figure states its weighting (source, date, members covered); the operator's dated population table fills only the members the stored series lacks
key_paths: src/stats/population.py; src/stats/aggregate.py; src/api/governments.py; src/static/app-gov-law.js; configs/external_artifacts.yml; tests/test_population_weighting.py
summary: Slice S06-04 S6, code and fixtures only. aggregate_indicator gains an optional weight_source and every weighted figure (and the missing_weight refusal) carries a weighting block: weight, stated, source, as_of, members_total, members_covered, members_without_weight, from_table, table. A weighting nobody described reads stated false, never an invented source. New src/stats/population.py loads configs/population_table.json (an operator drop-in, NOT shipped: source, as_of, rows of alpha-2 to population) and fills only holes in the stored SP.POP.TOTL series; a stored figure always wins; a table with no source, no usable as_of, a bad row (not a two-letter code, not a finite number above zero, a duplicate) is refused whole; an absent file changes nothing. A member with a value and no population anywhere is still a named refusal (no unweighted mean under the weighted label). The Governments tab draws the weighting as a visible caveat line (3 strings x12, non-English AI-drafted and flagged for native review). Registry entry population-table (optional until the operator places the file). NOT in this PR: the default-strategy change for intensive indicators with no exact weighting (a separate proposal), and the table itself (operator step: place configs/population_table.json).
